findings.summary: Task 2 Step 4 requires adding a comment to src/super_harness/core/review_bundle.py, which is not in the Declared scope list — and Task 2 itself tightens the verify baseline to exact set membership, so the file would be flagged by `verify` and produce a merge-gate blocker (`changed file not covered by any complete lifecycle`, engineering/attestation.py:297). It is also not a plan_artifact, so the pre-tool-use gate blocks the write in the gated state. Either declare the file in scope or drop Step 4 and keep the rationale in the design document, where it already is (design §1).

Guard Arm A (`refuse skip when no round has been frozen in the current epoch`) removes the escape hatch for any reviewer role configured with only human participants: `review begin` exits EXIT_VALIDATION with `<reviewer> has no automated participants` (cli/review.py:724-733), so no round can ever be frozen and no epoch round exists. The same coupling bites automated configs whose `review begin` fails for reasons independent of the reviewer (BundleError, dirty in-scope tree, governance load failure) — i.e. precisely the stuck states the hatch exists for. Suggest narrowing Arm A to roles that have automated participants, or replacing it with `refuse skip unless --override --reason` when no round was frozen (disclosure instead of refusal).

Task 2 leaves the `core/scope_match.py` module docstring stale: it states `covered_by_scope` was extracted from `sensors.verification_runner._covered_by_scope` and that `Task 2 re-points the baseline at this copy`, which stops being true once the baseline moves to canonical-path set membership. The file is not in the Declared scope, so fixing it needs a scope entry; if it is left as-is, say so explicitly (same doc-accuracy class as CODX-007 in the prior cut). Also note the local import alias is `_covered_by_scope` (verification_runner.py:57), not `covered_by_scope` as Task 2 Step 2 spells it.

findings.summary: The load-bearing rationale for the Arm A carve-out is factually wrong. The design (line 69-73) and implementation (Step 1, Arm A bullet) both assert that if Arm A fired unconditionally, "a human-only code-reviewer could then only ever be rejected — never passed", because there is "no CLI-reachable recovery from AWAITING_CODE_REVIEW". But `review human confirm` (cli/review.py:2182+) mints its own round_id/run_id at lines 2319-2320 and emits the round_started/result_imported/round_closed sequence without ever requiring `review begin` — so a human-only role passes through the interactive human workflow, which is exactly what `review begin`'s refusal hint at cli/review.py:730 tells the operator to use. The carve-out may still be defensible on other grounds (a human-only role can never have a frozen round, so unconditional Arm A would silently revoke the documented `skip --override` escape hatch for it), but as written the plan pins a test ("a human-only role can still be skipped") on a deadlock that does not exist, and the stated reason will mislead the implementer and any later reader deciding whether the carve-out is still needed. Restate the justification against the actual behaviour, or drop the carve-out if the human workflow is deemed the intended path.

Step 2 instructs "Reuse the automated-participant predicate from `review begin` rather than re-deriving it, so the two cannot drift", but no such predicate exists — the logic is an inline generator expression in the `begin` command body at cli/review.py:720-724. Following the instruction literally requires extracting a new module-level helper and rewriting `begin`'s call site, which the plan never states as a step; an implementer could equally read it as "call the same governance fields" and produce the duplication the sentence is trying to prevent. Name the extraction as an explicit edit.

checklist.note: Both prior-round items are addressed and the two docs stay consistent: design §3 and implementation Task 4 Step 1/Step 2 both describe Arm A as unconditional, the Definition of Done bullet flipped from 'still passes a human-only role' to 'refuses a human-only role', and no stale reference to the dropped carve-out remains (grepped automated|carve|human-only). Every code citation added by the delta checks out: begin's inline automated-participant genexp at cli/review.py:720-724 and refusal at 725-734; confirm's TTY refusal and no-self-confirm hint at 2189-2196; round_id/run_id minted at 2319-2320 without review begin. The claim that skip can today sidestep the human-confirm guard is also true — cli/review.py:502-556 has no human/automated or TTY check.

Dropping the carve-out is right — the old premise was false and the new refutation is verified (epoch boundaries come from plan_ready/code_review_requested in engineering/review_runs.py:135-144, not from review begin). But the replacement rationale rests on its own unstated precondition: that pass path requires an interactive TTY, and init's default governance is human-only, so the delta silently removes the last escape hatch for the default out-of-the-box config in any non-TTY agent-driven session. See DR3-01.

The delta touches only the two plan documents, both in the change's declared scope, and it removes rather than adds implementation surface (no automated-participant helper extraction, explicitly declared out of scope). DR3-01 notes the behaviour change may need an adopter-facing doc beyond the declared file list, but the delta itself declares nothing undeclared.

findings.summary: The new rationale for unconditional Arm A omits the precondition that makes it load-bearing. `review human confirm` is only reachable from an interactive TTY — it exits EXIT_VALIDATION on `not _interactive_terminal()` (cli/review.py:2189-2196) — and `review human draft` additionally requires a packet from `review prepare` (cli/review.py:2057). Meanwhile init's skeleton governance ships `participants: [human]` for BOTH plan-reviewer and code-reviewer (cli/init.py:207-215; the wizard path at 309-310 also defaults to `[human]` when no automated producer is selected). So for a default-config adopter driving the CLI through an agent (no TTY — the harness's own dogfood mode), the delta converts `review skip --override` from a disclosed, merge-gate-visible escape hatch into a hard refusal with no way to pass code-reviewer in that session; the only exit is `plan redeclare` back to INTENT_DECLARED plus a full plan cycle (d-no-recovery-from-awaiting-code-review). The design states the consequence only as 'closes a hole' and the implementation pins it only as a unit test; neither says the pass path needs a TTY, neither notes the default-governance impact, and no adopter-facing doc (docs/limitations.md, docs/adopting.md, or a note steering adopters to configure automated participants) is named in the plan or the declared scope — Step 4's cli-reference regeneration only covers the `--stuck-source` rename. Either state the TTY precondition plus the default-config consequence and declare the doc that records it, or reinstate a narrower allowance (e.g. permit `skip --override` when the role has no automated participants AND no TTY is available) with that reasoning written down.

The Step 2 hint specification is incomplete for the human path it now has to teach. It says to point at `review prepare` + `review begin` for the automated case and at `review human draft` / `review human confirm` for a human-owned role, but `human draft` reads the prepared packet (`_read_packet_or_exit`, cli/review.py:2057) and hard-fails without it, so the human path is `review prepare` → `review human draft` → `review human confirm`. As written an implementer can emit a hint whose first human-path step fails for the operator most likely to hit Arm A — someone who reached `skip` precisely because they never ran `prepare`/`begin`. Name `review prepare` in the human branch of the hint too.

The 'reuse the automated-participant predicate' instruction is gone; Step 2 now states no shared predicate is needed and records that begin's check is an inline generator expression at cli/review.py:720-724 (confirmed), with extraction explicitly out of scope. No unstated edit remains.

findings.summary: The delta's whole safeguard against the shared-decorator hazard is "Add a test asserting approve and reject still accept --source" (:188-189, restated in DoD :265 as "pinned by a test"), but as specified that test cannot fail. EXIT_VALIDATION is 2 (src/super_harness/exit_codes.py:14) and click also exits 2 on "No such option: --source"; approve (cli/review.py:458-467) and reject (:484-492) delete every option and exit 2 unconditionally through _block_direct_verdict_protocol. So the natural form — invoke `review approve <c> --reviewer plan-reviewer --source claude` and assert exit code 2 — passes identically whether the flag exists or was removed, i.e. a future edit that does rename _source_opt at the definition site would ship green. The plan must specify the discriminating assertion: match the fail-loud message on stderr (or assert `--source` appears in `review approve --help` / `review reject --help`) and assert that "No such option" does not.

Step 4 now prescribes an inline `click.option("--stuck-source", ...)` on skip but says nothing about the two things that rename forces inside the function: click derives the parameter name `stuck_source`, so skip's signature (cli/review.py:509-512) and its governance-participant validation block (:530-548) must be rethreaded, and the emitted audit payload currently stamps `extra["source"] = source` (:548). Whether that event key stays "source" or becomes "stuck_source" is left to the implementer's guess. Failure scenario: the implementer renames the payload key for symmetry, and the append-only stream then carries two different keys for the same audit fact — every past skip (twelve in the previous cut) under "source", every future one under "stuck_source" — so any later reader of skipped-review attribution must special-case both, permanently. State explicitly that the flag is renamed while the recorded payload key stays `source`, and that the participant validation is retained.
